run.target: SINGLE Business Tenant + Party Actor + federated identity foundation

rows.action: Resolve registration, Tenant provisioning and Party creation policies on the server
rows.assertion: SINGLE forces Tenant provisioning disabled and retains legacy registration compatibility without allowing it to weaken explicit policy

rows.action: Admit an allowed identity into the server-owned Default Business Tenant
rows.assertion: SINGLE creates/reuses the business TenantMember, rejects CLOSED registration and never selects System Tenant

rows.action: Block create/join/select product entry in SINGLE while preserving MULTI self-service
rows.assertion: Direct API calls are rejected in SINGLE; registration, OTP and password login bypass Tenant selection; MULTI registration/login still enters the existing space-selection journey

rows.action: Enforce Tenant create and join policy below the controller boundary
rows.assertion: Service callers cannot create a Tenant when provisioning is disabled or join another Tenant in SINGLE mode

groups.title: Complete Party and IAM data model

rows.action: Migrate Party 12 tables, IAM 5 tables, role scope and session context fields
rows.assertion: Fresh PostgreSQL reaches migration v20260809120000 and model round-trips without schema drift

rows.action: Keep Party persistence tenant-filtered with composite tenant foreign keys
rows.assertion: Party mapper observes current tenant and schema prevents cross-tenant membership/session references

rows.action: Resolve and repair the default LoginApplication/Channel/AuthMethod
rows.assertion: Schema-snapshot first install receives separate Web/native default password surfaces; tenant toggles control built-in password/OTP methods while canonical registry controls federated IdP methods

rows.action: Manage external IdP instances and orchestrate OAuth/LDAP federation through the canonical registry
rows.assertion: Management API, channel binding, canonical external links and runtime orchestration are active while legacy social paths remain compatible; a full visual IdP administration console is a non-goal

groups.title: Party lifecycle, authorization and Actor session

rows.action: Create a Party under approval policy and activate it
rows.assertion: Approval-required creates pending Party/Membership; approval makes the Actor eligible

rows.action: Switch to an active Party Actor
rows.assertion: Replacement session is minted before old revoke; new token is ready/party with cv increment, old token is rejected

rows.action: Evaluate active membership, PARTY role, capability and resource ownership
rows.assertion: Only the selected active Actor contributes PARTY roles; capability remains distinct; cross-Party resource access is denied

rows.action: Filter Actor candidates by the current application/channel Party capabilities
rows.assertion: Only active Parties with an allowed capability are eligible; disabled, half-bound or cross-tenant channels fail closed; global channels remain valid

rows.action: Run generic invitation, capability approval, relation and business-network workflows
rows.assertion: Full model exists; general-purpose workflow/UI is intentionally deferred until a concrete domain needs it

groups.title: Federated identity registry, OAuth/OIDC/WeChat/LDAP and native clients

rows.action: Resolve separate Web/mobile login applications, channels and IdP instances in SINGLE mode
rows.assertion: Fresh PostgreSQL bootstrap repairs both surfaces; same provider code can be independently enabled per application and SINGLE tenant is server-owned

rows.action: Create and consume one-time state/nonce/PKCE transactions bound to Web cookies or native secrets
rows.assertion: Redis stores only the binding digest; wrong or missing binding and platform mismatch fail closed, consume the state, and cannot be replayed

rows.action: Run OIDC, WeChat Website, Apple Web and LDAP protocol/security contracts
rows.assertion: OIDC URL/claim hardening, WeChat openid contract, Apple query-code callback and real TCP/JNDI LDAP immutable identity are executable and green

rows.action: Render a configured IdP, start OAuth, reject forged state, preserve password login and show authenticated binding UI
rows.assertion: Real browser reached Google authorize, rejects state mismatch before exchange, consumes state, blocks empty merge confirmation, routes SINGLE to the workspace and MULTI to Tenant selection, while authenticated binding remains executable
rows.vision_check: Inspected semantic DOM and rendered pixels for the login and social-binding pages on the PostgreSQL/Redis runtime

rows.action: Complete an external Google/OIDC and WeChat login with real provider credentials
rows.assertion: Official Google authorize is reachable with an intentionally invalid client, but Google/WeChat/WeCom/OIDC/Microsoft credentials are absent and the known runtime databases contain no OAuth CloudConfig credentials, so no real token exchange was performed

rows.action: Complete mobile-channel deep-link/state/native-binding login on iOS and Android physical devices
rows.assertion: Native unit tests pass (Android 39/39, iOS 4/4) and the dynamic OAuth UI passes against the real backend on an Android emulator 3/3 and iOS Simulator 3/3; Android has no physical device, while the paired iPhone build is blocked by its signing certificate and four provisioning profiles, so no physical install/login occurred

groups.title: Web journey, SQL performance and falsifiability

rows.action: Log in to the unique business workspace and switch Business identity from the Header
rows.assertion: No registration/Tenant self-service entry; Actor switch persists and current Actor is visibly selected; console has no errors
rows.vision_check: Manually inspected login, /home, user menu, switch result and browser console in isolated runtime

rows.action: Query Party by fixed tenant and lifecycle at realistic fixture cardinality
rows.assertion: PostgreSQL uses idx_party_tenant_status; 20k-row transactional fixture is fully rolled back

rows.action: Remove tenant/member context before Party revalidation, observe red, restore and rerun
rows.assertion: Controlled mutation fails the crown-jewel test and restored code passes targeted plus final combined suite
